sections.heading: What a DWLI Charge Means in Texas
paragraphs: "Driving while license invalid" is the Texas name for driving on a suspended, revoked, cancelled or denied license — Transportation Code 521.457. Many El Paso drivers who get this ticket did not know their license was invalid: a stop on Gateway East for a tail light, a license check, and the DPS computer comes back "suspended" because of something from a year or two ago.

A basic DWLI is a Class C misdemeanor: a fine of up to $500 plus court costs, no jail, filed in municipal or Justice of the Peace court like any other ticket. But the statute has teeth. It becomes a Class B misdemeanor, punishable by up to 180 days in county jail and a fine of up to $2,000, if you have a prior DWLI conviction, if you were driving without the liability insurance Section 601.191 requires, or if your license was suspended because of an intoxication offense. It becomes a Class A misdemeanor if you were uninsured and caused or were at fault in a crash that resulted in serious bodily injury or death. Class A and B cases are filed in the County Courts at Law at the El Paso County Courthouse, 500 E. San Antonio Ave, and create a full criminal record.

That is why the first DWLI matters, and why the insurance question matters alongside it. If a DWLI ends in a conviction, every future stop while your license is still tangled is a potential jail case. If it ends in a dismissal or deferred disposition, there is nothing to enhance. This page is general information, not legal advice about your case.

sections.heading: Fix the License First: How We Approach a DWLI Ticket
paragraphs: When you hire us online or call 915-503-1600, we file a notice of appearance promptly so the DWLI case can't go to warrant while we work. Then we attack the cause. If it's an OMNI hold, we resolve the underlying ticket — often with a warrant recall and a negotiated disposition — and ask the court to release the hold. If it's a DPS suspension, we check whether the period has already run and whether a reinstatement fee is all that remains.

Once DPS shows the license as valid, we walk into the pretrial docket with that proof. Prosecutors in El Paso Municipal Court and the JP precincts know many DWLI defendants got lost in the system, and many will consider a dismissal or deferred disposition for a driver who has cleaned up the problem. Where the license can't be restored quickly, we ask for deferred disposition anyway so the case can end in dismissal rather than a conviction.

For drivers whose suspension still has months to run, an occupational driver's license is often the right move: a court-ordered restricted license under Transportation Code Chapter 521, Subchapter L that lets you drive to work, school and essential errands while the suspension finishes.

sections.heading: Class C vs. Class B: Where Your DWLI Case Will Be Heard
paragraphs: A Class C DWLI from El Paso Police is filed in El Paso Municipal Court ($59). One from a DPS trooper, deputy or constable goes to a Justice of the Peace precinct, and Horizon City, Socorro, San Elizario, Clint and Anthony tickets go to their municipal courts ($69). In all of them, you generally do not need to appear unless the case is set for trial.

If the officer charged the Class B or Class A version — because of a prior DWLI, no insurance at the time of the stop, an intoxication-related suspension, or an injury crash — the case is prosecuted by the County Attorney at the County Courthouse. That is a different kind of case with a different fee — and exactly what handling the first ticket properly is meant to avoid. If you were arrested rather than cited, call us before your first setting; whether the "prior" is really a conviction often decides these cases.

sections.heading: Don't Pay a DWLI Ticket Before You Read This
paragraphs: Paying a DWLI ticket online is a guilty plea, and a DWLI conviction is the one thing that can turn your next ticket into a jail case. It also does nothing about the suspension: the license stays invalid and the cycle repeats. Instead, check the appearance date on your citation, don't miss it, and send us the ticket through the online hire form. The free ticket and warrant lookup will show whether an earlier case already has a warrant.

faqs.q: Is driving while license invalid a jailable offense in Texas?
faqs.a: A basic DWLI under Transportation Code 521.457 is a Class C misdemeanor — fine only, no jail. It becomes a Class B, with up to 180 days in jail, if you have a prior DWLI conviction, were driving without insurance at the time, or were suspended for an intoxication offense; and a Class A if you were uninsured and caused a crash with serious injury or death.

faqs.q: I didn't know my license was suspended. Is that a defense?
faqs.a: It helps, and it's common — DPS mails notices to addresses that are often years out of date. It also tells us where to look: an OMNI hold, an old ticket, or a suspension that may have already expired.

faqs.q: What is an OMNI hold and how does it cause a DWLI?
faqs.a: OMNI is the Failure to Appear program under Transportation Code Chapter 706. When a court reports an unresolved ticket, DPS refuses to renew your license. If your license then expires and you keep driving, the next stop can be a DWLI. Clearing the ticket releases the hold — see our OMNI hold removal page.

faqs.q: Can I get an occupational license while my DWLI case is pending?
faqs.a: Often, yes. An occupational driver's license is a court-ordered restricted license that lets you drive for work, school and household needs during a suspension. We handle those petitions in El Paso County; see our occupational driver's license page.

faqs.q: Will I have to go to court for a Class C DWLI?
faqs.a: Generally not. We appear for you in El Paso Municipal Court, the JP precincts and the area city courts and handle the pretrial negotiation. You would only appear if the case went to trial, which is uncommon and something we discuss with you first.

faqs.q: What does it cost to hire you for a DWLI ticket?
faqs.a: $59 for El Paso Municipal Court and $69 for JP, Horizon City, Socorro, San Elizario, Clint and Anthony courts. Additional citations from the same stop are discounted add-ons; related warrants are $35 for the first and $20 each after that.
